summary: The endpoint-disjoint matching and accepted endpoint-capacity inequality give each of the two central endpoint classes mass at most t_0, hence H_star <= 2t_0, and the accepted strict dyadic cap yields the claimed strict upper bound. The comparison gamma_d <= 1/2 is valid for every integer d >= 1, so the selected-mass packet bound cannot meet the hard contradiction threshold. For the exact lattice energy, terminality indeed forces the stated strict amplification gap after subtracting the strict H_star cap. The argument handles empty endpoint classes, equality thresholds, and the smallest case n=2, d=1, and it invokes the predecessor facts only under their stated hypotheses.
